title: Giant Pterosaur Behavior
content: New theories have emerged about the behavior of giant pterosaurs.A team of researchers at Johns Hopkins has concluded that most pterosaurs probably didn’t take off by running on their back legs and flapping, the way birds do. They used all four appendages pushing off the ground to propel them into flight.Link for the Science Daily story.Scientists at the University of Sheffield have argued that large pterosaurs probably didn’t feed while skimming their bill along the surface of the water.Link.And finally, a group of scientists at the University of Portsmouth have concluded that large pterosaurs related to the Quetzalcoatlus probably spent a lot of time walking around as “specialized terrestrial stalkers” and may not have spent much of their time flying.Link.Images are from Dinotopia: Journey to Chandara,link.Thanks, Steve B!
